messages:
sarah: Hey @runtime-team @jess — opened a docs PR that documents the prefetch cache TTL behavior and shows an SDK snippet. I'm not 100% sure the wording matches the runtime. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/412

jess: Thanks — adding reviewers. Can we hold merge until runtime confirms the exact semantics? This is likely to confuse customers if the default differs by deployment.

devex-ci-bot: Docs preview deployed: https://preview.redwood.dev/pr-412 (build 248) 

tomas: Looking. Quick Q: which example are you using in the PR? Dedicated/private behaviors differ a bit for cache enforcement.

sarah: The JS SDK snippet in the PR — shows setting prefetch_ttl: 60 on a route and says "prefetch will respect TTL". Example from PR:
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.routes.update('search-route', { prefetch_ttl: 60 });
```
We intended to document that the SDK-specified TTL is what the platform uses, but someone on eng pointed out dedicated pools might enforce a minimum.

liam: Confirming — runtime currently enforces a 120s minimum on Dedicated pools to avoid thrash. Private/VPC inherits customer config (no minimum). Hosted (shared) defaults to 60 if not overridden.

tomas: Right. Runtime treats prefetch_ttl as a hint for hosted and private, but Dedicated has an enforced floor (120s) to stabilize batching. I should've flagged this earlier.

jess: OK that's the crux. Docs should call out the deployment differences (Hosted/Private vs Dedicated minimum). Also add a note with guidance: "If you rely on sub-120s TTL on Dedicated, contact support or use a different route config."

sarah: I can add that wording. Do we want me to mention the exact number (120s) or say "enforced minimum higher than hosted"?

tomas: Put the exact number for now (120s) — we'll keep that in sync. I'm going to open a runtime issue to track possibly making the floor configurable for dedicated customers: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/889. I'll link here when it's created.

jess: Please add the issue link in the PR description so reviewers can see it's tracked. Until runtime signs off on the text, please don't merge.

sarah: Will do. Adding a note in the PR and updating the snippet to explicitly show the behavior for each deployment.

devex-ci-bot: Linkcheck passed for PR 412.

tomas: Filed the runtime issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/889 — summary: "enforce minimum prefetch_ttl for Dedicated pools (120s) and expose config flag for enterprise customers." I added a label `docs-action` and will post an engineering PR next week for the flag.

jess: Great, thanks. I'm assigning reviewers: @liam, @jess. After runtime PR lands we'll re-evaluate. :thumbsup:

sarah: Thanks everyone — holding merge until runtime confirms. I'll update PR now with the exact wording and the runtime issue link.

liam: Quick nit: in the SDK snippet you might also show the server-side YAML example, customers look for both.

sarah: Good call, adding that as well.

jess: Echoing — thanks. We'll re-open the review once the PR has the issue link and the added YAML example.

sarah: Done — PR updated with runtime issue link and YAML example. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/412#issuecomment-551

devex-ci-bot: Docs preview updated: https://preview.redwood.dev/pr-412 (build 249)

jess: Reviewing the new wording now. If everything looks good I'll queue it for merge after runtime signs off on the engineering issue.

sarah: Closing the loop here — thanks all for the quick turnaround.
